description: Semantic manifest of Coinbase Advanced public REST API behavior, distilled from a single real discovery run. No raw payloads; see provenance for the evidence directory.

request_format.granularity: ONE_DAY accepted for all candle requests; both products.
request_format.start_end_encoding: start/end sent as Unix-seconds strings (e.g. "1791209606") and accepted. Other encodings (ISO, integers) were not tested.

candle_bucket_alignment.rule: Every returned candle.start is UTC midnight (start % 86400 == 0).
candle_bucket_alignment.evidence: All 720 returned candle starts across 05,06,09,10,12,13 have modulo 86400 == 0 (verified programmatically); candle.start labels the start of the day bucket.

candle_ordering.rule: Candles are returned newest-first (descending by start).
candle_ordering.evidence: 05_recent_candles_ADA-EUR.json and 06_recent_candles_DOT-EUR.json both descend from 2026-10-15 to 2026-10-06; same pattern in 09/10/12/13.

partial_current_day_included.rule: The bucket containing the request's `end` is returned even when incomplete.
partial_current_day_included.evidence: Run executed ~14:13 UTC on 2026-10-15; newest candle in 05 and 06 has start=1792022400 (2026-10-15T00:00:00Z), i.e. today's partial day, confirmed by summary.json's newest_candle_start_is_on_run_start_utc_date=true for both.

window_boundary_artifact.rule: Only buckets with start >= request start are returned; the UTC day containing a non-midnight request `start` is excluded, not a real gap.
window_boundary_artifact.evidence: Every candle probe's missing_daily_buckets_utc in summary.json is a single entry equal to the UTC day containing that probe's request start: 2026-10-05 for 05/06 (start=1791209606, mid-day), 2024-11-14 for 09 (300-day window), 2024-09-25 for 10/12/13 (350-day windows). returned_candle_count == requested_calendar_day_count exactly in every successful probe, confirming no other gaps exist once this boundary day is accounted for.

request_size_limit.rule: 350 daily candles per request succeeds; 351 is rejected with HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT.
request_size_limit.evidence: 09 (300 days) and 10 (350 days) both outcome=ok with returned_candle_count == requested days. 11 (351 days) outcome=error, status_code=400, exception_class=HTTPError, server message verbatim: "start and end argument is invalid - number of candles requested should be less than 350".
request_size_limit.note: The server's own wording ("less than 350") is imprecise relative to observed behavior: 350 itself succeeds, so the true accepted range is <= 350, not < 350. Record the message verbatim but do not trust its literal wording over the empirical result.

pre_listing_window.rule: A candle window entirely before a product's tradable history returns an empty candle list with outcome=ok, no error.

candle_field_types.rule: All candle OHLCV fields (open, high, low, close, volume) are decimal strings, never JSON numbers.
candle_field_types.evidence: Verified in 05, 06, 09, 10, 12, 13 — every candle field is a quoted string (e.g. "close": "0.199", "volume": "1651833.93").

no_real_gaps_in_350_day_windows.rule: No missing days in the 300/350-day windows for either product beyond the single window-boundary artifact.
no_real_gaps_in_350_day_windows.evidence: 09, 10, 12, 13 each have exactly one missing_daily_buckets_utc entry (the boundary day) and returned_candle_count == requested_calendar_day_count.

server_time_fields.rule: get_unix_time returns epoch_seconds and epoch_millis as strings plus an iso field. Observed local-vs-server offset was sub-second (+0.046 s at start, -0.492 s at end); its cause is not determined.
server_time_fields.evidence: 02_server_time_start.json: epoch_seconds="1792073607", epoch_millis="1792073607208", iso="2026-10-15T14:13:27Z", elapsed_milliseconds=308. 14_server_time_end.json: epoch_seconds="1792073621", iso="2026-10-15T14:13:41Z", elapsed_milliseconds=128. Computed offsets: start +0.046s, end -0.492s.

both_products.new_at: 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z (identical for both products; NOT evidence of actual listing/history start date, see open_questions)

candle_volume_is_in_base_units.claim: Candle `volume` (and product `volume_24h`) are denominated in the base currency (ADA, DOT), not the quote currency (EUR).
candle_volume_is_in_base_units.basis: volume_24h * price reproduces approximate_quote_24h_volume almost exactly for both products: ADA-EUR 2336220.54 * 0.199 = 464907.88746 (matches approximate_quote_24h_volume exactly); DOT-EUR 199462.201 * 0.9602 = 191523.6054 (matches exactly). Candle volumes (e.g. ADA-EUR ~1.1M-3.5M per day) are the same order of magnitude as volume_24h (2.34M), consistent with base-unit denomination.
candle_volume_is_in_base_units.confidence: INFERRED, not directly confirmed by any field that explicitly states units; the arithmetic match across two independent products is strong corroborating evidence but the API never labels volume's currency explicitly.

open_questions: Earliest available daily candle per product (ADA-EUR, DOT-EUR) — not determined by this run; to be found during M5b ingestion by paging the candle endpoint backward in <=350-day windows until an empty response is returned.

Public (unauthenticated) endpoint rate limits — not observed in this run (13 requests at >=1.0s spacing); no HTTP 429 observed; response headers were not recorded. The actual limit and window are unknown.
Duplicate-timestamp behavior — not observed; unknown whether the API can ever return two candles with the same `start` for one request, or how overlapping-window requests reconcile.
Historical revision behavior — not observed; unknown whether previously-returned candle values (especially for the most recent, partial day) can change on a later request for the same window.
